i.norm: Verifies that calling hasNext() on a nested FilterListIterator exhausts the underlying iterator, and that hasPrevious() returns false because no element has been returned via next() yet (the iterator position has not advanced). Setup: a single-element list whose element matches the inner filter predicate (EqualPredicate) and also passes the outer filter predicate (UniquePredicate). The outer FilterListIterator wraps an inner FilterListIterator which itself wraps the raw ListIterator.
Build a single-element list and obtain its ListIterator
Inner filter: only pass elements equal to targetObject
Outer filter: only pass elements seen for the first time (uniqueness filter)
Calling hasNext() causes the outer iterator to scan forward through the chain, consuming the single element from the underlying rawListIterator in the process.
The underlying raw iterator has been fully consumed by the hasNext() scan above
hasPrevious() returns false: no element has been returned via next() yet, so the logical position has not advanced and there is nothing to go back to.
